# ERP API Token Manager

> A self-hosted Bearer-token lifecycle manager embedded inside an existing .NET ERP — lets ERP users create, list, and revoke API tokens through a Razor Pages UI, with three POC business endpoints ready for N8N automation workflows.

## Overview

**ERP API Token Manager** is a Bearer-token lifecycle module embedded directly inside an existing .NET ERP application. It eliminates the 2-10 working day wait time that ERP business users currently experience when integrating low-code automation tools (N8N, Make, Zapier) with internal ERP APIs.

It was built to solve **the absence of a self-service API authentication layer in mid-size .NET ERP systems** — a gap that matters to **ERP IT Admins, business analysts running N8N workflows, and IT junior operators** because the status quo (shared Basic-Auth credentials, IT-issued integration tickets, or unauthenticated endpoints) silently leaks credentials, blocks automation projects, and produces no audit trail.

The project is governed by the upstream documents below; every design decision maps to a tracked requirement:

| Document | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| [IDEA](docs/IDEA.md) | Problem framing, leap-of-faith assumptions, market intelligence |
| [BRD](docs/BRD.md) | PR-FAQ, business goals, ROI, MoSCoW, RACI, sign-off |
| [PRD](docs/PRD.md) | User stories, acceptance criteria, P0/P1/P2 priority tiers |
| [PDD](docs/PDD.md) | UX flows, screen specs, interaction patterns |
| [EDD](docs/EDD.md) | Architecture decisions, technology choices, data models |
| [ARCH](docs/ARCH.md) | C4 diagrams, deployment topology, ADRs |

See [System Architecture](#system-architecture) below for a visual overview, or the full [HTML documentation site](docs/pages/index.html) for navigable reference.

## Core Features

**P0 — Must ship for v1.0:**

- **F-AUTH-01 · Token Creation** — Self-service UI for creating Bearer tokens. The raw `tk_<32 chars>` value is shown **once**; only its SHA-256 hash and 11-char prefix are persisted.
- **F-AUTH-02 · Token Listing** — Per-user token list showing prefix, description, status, created/last-used timestamps. IT Admins see all users' tokens with `?userId=` filter.
- **F-AUTH-03 · Token Revocation** — Immediate (no-cache) revocation. Once revoked, the next API call with that token returns HTTP 401 — verified by integration tests at < 100 ms latency.
- **F-AUTH-04 · Bearer Auth Middleware** — Custom `AuthenticationHandler<>` validates `Authorization: Bearer tk_…` against the live database on every request. No in-memory cache → revocation is instant.
- **F-DEMO-01/02/03 · POC Business Endpoints** — Three real-shape ERP endpoints for N8N integration:
  - `GET /api/v1/demo/sales` — daily sales rollup
  - `GET /api/v1/demo/inventory` — current stock levels
  - `GET /api/v1/demo/orders/{orderId}` — order status by ID
- **F-SEC-01 · Hashed Storage** — SHA-256 hex (64 chars) is the only token representation in the database. Plaintext appears only in the HTTP response on creation and is never logged.

**P1 — MVP-mandatory, ships with P0:**

- **F-AUDIT-01 · Audit Log** — Every `Create` and `Revoke` event records timestamp, operator user-id, token prefix, and client IP (auto-masked after 90 days for GDPR).
- **F-SEC-02 · HTTPS Enforcement** — HSTS header issued by the ASP.NET Core pipeline; reverse-proxy NGINX terminates TLS in production.
- **Rate Limiting** — 60 req/min on `/api/v1/me/tokens`, 120 req/min on `/api/v1/demo/*` (Fixed Window per Token / IP / endpoint group).
- **CSRF Protection** — Anti-forgery tokens on all state-changing Razor Pages forms.
- **Feature Flag** — `ENABLE_POC_DEMO_APIS=false` removes the POC routes entirely (compile-time route filter).

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

All paths share these requirements:

- [Git](https://git-scm.com/) 2.40+
- An `.env` file — copy from `.env.example` (see [Environment Variables](#environment-variables))

### Docker (Recommended)

The fastest path to a running stack. `docker compose` boots the .NET app and PostgreSQL with health-check ordering.

**Prerequisites:** [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) 24+ (includes Compose v2)

```bash
git clone https://git.ouryahoo.com/tobala/erp-api-token-manager.git
cd erp-api-token-manager

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env — set POSTGRES_PASSWORD and ENABLE_POC_DEMO_APIS=true

# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Confirm everything is healthy
docker compose ps
# Expected: all services show "running (healthy)"
```

Verify the app is responding:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/demo/health
# {"status":"ok","version":"1.0.0","uptime_seconds":3}
```

Open the Razor Pages UI:

```bash
open http://localhost:8080/ApiTokens
```

---

### macOS / Linux (Native .NET)

Use this path when you want to run the ASP.NET Core process directly for live-reload development.

**Prerequisites:**

- [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) (8.0.300+)
- PostgreSQL 16+ (local) or a remote `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` value
- Optional: `dotnet-ef` global tool for migrations (`dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef`)

```bash
git clone https://git.ouryahoo.com/tobala/erp-api-token-manager.git
cd erp-api-token-manager

# Restore packages
dotnet restore

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your local PostgreSQL credentials

# Apply database migrations
dotnet ef database update --project src/ErpApiTokenManager

# Run the development server
dotnet run --project src/ErpApiTokenManager --launch-profile Development
```

Expected output:

```
[ERP-API-Token-Manager] Now listening on: http://localhost:8080
[ERP-API-Token-Manager] Database: connected (Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=erpapikey)
[ERP-API-Token-Manager] Application started. Press Ctrl+C to shut down.
```

---

### Windows (PowerShell)

> **Recommendation:** Use [WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/install) + Docker Desktop for the smoothest experience. The commands below also work in PowerShell 7+ natively.

**Prerequisites:** Same .NET 8 SDK + PostgreSQL 16 requirements as macOS/Linux above. Install via [winget](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/):

```powershell
winget install Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.8
winget install PostgreSQL.PostgreSQL.16
```

Run the app:

```powershell

Set-Location erp-api-token-manager

# Open .env in your editor and fill in PostgreSQL credentials

dotnet ef database update --project src/ErpApiTokenManager
dotnet run --project src/ErpApiTokenManager --launch-profile Development
```

Verify the server started:

```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:8080/api/v1/demo/health
```

## Environment Variables

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` before starting the application. The app validates all required variables at startup and exits with a clear error if any are missing.

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|----------|-------------|----------|---------|---------|
| `POSTGRES_USER` | PostgreSQL username for the application database | Yes | `erpuser` | `erpuser` |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | PostgreSQL password (must be ≥ 16 chars in production) | **Yes** | — | `s3cr3t-at-least-32-chars` |
| `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` | Full PostgreSQL connection string (overrides `POSTGRES_*`) | No | derived | `Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=erpapikey;Username=erpuser;Password=...` |
| `ENABLE_POC_DEMO_APIS` | Toggle the `/api/v1/demo/*` POC routes (set `true` for the demo) | No | `false` | `true` |
| `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` | ASP.NET Core hosting environment | No | `Production` | `Development`, `Staging`, `Production` |
| `ASPNETCORE_URLS` | Listener URLs for Kestrel | No | `http://+:8080` | `http://+:5000;https://+:5001` |
| `AppSettings__TokenHashAlgorithm` | Hash algorithm for tokens (locked to SHA256 in MVP) | No | `SHA256` | `SHA256` |
| `AppSettings__RateLimiting__TokenCreateMaxRequests` | Max token-create requests per window | No | `60` | `60` |
| `AppSettings__RateLimiting__TokenCreateWindowSeconds` | Window length in seconds | No | `60` | `60` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | OpenTelemetry OTLP collector endpoint | No | — | `http://otel-collector:4317` |

See [.env.example](.env.example) for the annotated template and [docs/EDD.md §17 Configuration Management](docs/EDD.md#17--configuration-management) for the complete reference.

## API Quick Reference

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1`. Token-management endpoints use ERP session cookies (Razor); POC endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <raw-token>`.

| Method + Path | Auth | Description |
|---------------|------|-------------|
| `POST /api/v1/me/tokens` | Cookie / Session | Create a new API token (raw value returned **once**) |
| `GET /api/v1/me/tokens` | Cookie / Session | List the current user's tokens (cursor pagination) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/tokens/{tokenId}` | Cookie / Session | Revoke a token (immediate, no cache) |
| `GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs` | Cookie + `is_superuser` | IT-Admin-only audit log query (page/sort/filter) |
| `GET /api/v1/demo/sales` | Bearer Token | POC: daily sales rollup |
| `GET /api/v1/demo/inventory` | Bearer Token | POC: current stock levels |
| `GET /api/v1/demo/orders/{orderId}/status` | Bearer Token | POC: single-order status |

For request/response schemas, error codes, rate limits, idempotency, pagination, and the OpenAPI 3.1 specification see:

- Markdown source: [docs/API.md](docs/API.md)
- Generated OpenAPI: [docs/blueprint/contracts/openapi.yaml](docs/blueprint/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- HTML reference: [docs/pages/api.html](docs/pages/api.html)

## Token Usage (N8N Integration)

The end-to-end flow for an N8N operator:

1. **Create a token in the ERP UI** — open `http://localhost:8080/ApiTokens`, click **建立 Token**, fill in a description, copy the raw `tk_<32 chars>` value shown once on the success screen.
2. **Configure the N8N HTTP Request node** — open the workflow, edit the HTTP Request node, set:
   - Authentication: **Header Auth**
   - Header name: `Authorization`
   - Header value: `Bearer <your-raw-token>`
3. **Call a POC endpoint:**

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tk_a1b2c3d4xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
     http://localhost:8080/api/v1/demo/sales
```

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tk_a1b2c3d4xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
     http://localhost:8080/api/v1/demo/orders/42
```

**Response on revoked token:**

```json
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "type": "https://erp.example.com/errors/invalid-token",
  "title": "Token revoked or invalid",
  "status": 401,
  "detail": "The presented bearer token was not found or has been revoked."
}
```

> Tokens are validated by hashing the incoming value (SHA-256) and comparing it to the stored digest on **every** request. There is no in-memory cache → revocation is instant.

For the full N8N walk-through (workflow templates, error-recovery patterns, credential rotation), see [docs/EDD.md §20 N8N Integration Guide](docs/EDD.md#20--n8n-integration-guide).

| `chore/<TICKET-ID>-short-description` | Tooling and maintenance | Yes (author) |

### Commit Message Format

This project follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```
<type>(<scope>): <short summary in imperative mood>

[optional body — what and why, not how]

[optional footer — BREAKING CHANGE, closes #issue]
```

Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `test`, `refactor`, `chore`, `perf`, `ci`

Examples:

```
feat(auth): add per-token rate limit budget configuration
fix(auth): reject Authorization headers without "Bearer " prefix
docs(readme): regenerate from upstream BRD/PRD/EDD via gendoc readme
```

### Pull Request Checklist

Before requesting review, confirm all of the following:

- [ ] All CI checks are green (build, lint, type-check, tests)
- [ ] Coverage has not dropped below 80%
- [ ] New or changed public API behavior is documented in `docs/API.md`
- [ ] Breaking changes include a migration note and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer
- [ ] Relevant `docs/` files (EDD, SCHEMA, RTM) are updated if the implementation changed
- [ ] The PR description explains *why* the change is needed, not just *what* it does

## Deployment

### Staging

Staging deploys automatically on every merge to `develop`. The pipeline runs the full test suite, builds the Docker image, pushes it to the registry, and triggers a Kubernetes rolling update.

```bash
# Trigger a manual staging deploy (GitHub Actions on git.ouryahoo.com)
gh workflow run deploy.yml -f environment=staging -f ref=develop
```

### Production

Production deploys are triggered by tagging a release on `main`:

```bash
git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0
```

The CI pipeline promotes the staging image (already tested) to production without a rebuild.

### Rollback

If a production issue is detected:

```bash
# Identify the previous stable image tag
gh release list --limit 5

# Roll back the Kubernetes deployment
kubectl set image deployment/erp-api-token-manager \
  app=erp-api-token-manager:1.0.0 \
  -n erp-prod

# Verify pods are healthy
kubectl rollout status deployment/erp-api-token-manager -n erp-prod
```

For detailed rollback steps including database migrations see [docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md) and [docs/EDD.md §22 Disaster Recovery](docs/EDD.md#22--disaster-recovery-dr-design).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| `Npgsql.PostgresException: 28P01: password authentication failed` on startup | `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` mismatch between app and database | Check `.env`, regenerate the password, restart with `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d` (⚠ wipes volumes) |
| `404 Not Found` on `/api/v1/demo/sales` | `ENABLE_POC_DEMO_APIS=false` (POC routes are compile-time-filtered) | Set `ENABLE_POC_DEMO_APIS=true` in `.env`, restart the app |
| `401 Unauthorized` on a freshly created token | Token has `tk_` prefix included only in display, not in the raw value | Use the **entire** raw token string from the success screen (including the `tk_` prefix) as the Bearer value |
| Razor Pages anti-forgery error (`400 Bad Request — A required anti-forgery token was not supplied`) | Form was submitted without the `__RequestVerificationToken` hidden field | Ensure the form has `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` (or use the `<form>` tag helper); do not POST via curl without first fetching the token |
| Docker Compose: `app` container restarts repeatedly with `Connection refused` | App started before PostgreSQL was healthy | Compose `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` should prevent this; if it persists, check `docker compose logs postgres` for migration init errors |
| `dotnet ef database update` fails with `relation "api_tokens" already exists` | Migrations ran twice against an existing volume | Drop the schema (`docker compose exec postgres psql -U erpuser -d erpapikey -c "DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;"`) and re-run migrations |

For issues not listed here, search [existing GitHub Issues](https://git.ouryahoo.com/tobala/erp-api-token-manager/issues) before opening a new one.

## Known Limitations

These are explicit MVP-scope decisions, not bugs (see [PRD §4.3 Out of Scope](docs/PRD.md#4-scope) and [BRD §15 Decisions](docs/BRD.md)):

- **No fine-grained Token scope/permissions** — every active token has full access to every protected endpoint. Scope-based authorization is deferred to v2.0 (would require an OAuth2 Resource Server architecture).
- **No automatic token rotation** — tokens are valid until manually revoked. The `ExpiresAt` column exists on the schema but is not enforced in MVP.
- **No external Identity Provider integration** — Keycloak / IdentityServer / Auth0 are explicitly out of scope to preserve the "zero external dependency" core differentiator.
- **No N8N native credential plugin** — N8N operators paste the raw token into the standard Header-Auth credential. A native plugin is a v2.0 candidate.
- **No token expiry email/notification system** — would require additional notification infrastructure; deferred to post-Pilot evaluation.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please read this section before submitting a pull request.

### Fork and PR Flow

1. Fork the repository on `git.ouryahoo.com`
2. Create a feature branch from `develop`: `git checkout -b feature/your-feature develop`
3. Write tests first (TDD) — the test suite must stay green
4. Commit using the Conventional Commits format described in [Development Workflow](#development-workflow)
5. Push your branch and open a PR against `develop` (not `main`)
6. Address all review feedback; request re-review after each update

### Code Style

- C# code is formatted by `dotnet format` on save (configured in `.editorconfig`)
- Lint rules are enforced by `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` (set as errors on `Domain` and `Application`)
- Type-checking happens at compile time — the CI blocks on warnings escalated to errors
- Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` locally before committing to avoid CI failures

### Issue Templates

Use the issue templates in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:

- **Bug report** — reproduction steps, expected vs actual behavior, environment details
- **Feature request** — problem statement, proposed solution, acceptance criteria
- **Documentation gap** — which document, what is missing or wrong

## Security Policy

If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not** open a public Issue.

**Responsible Disclosure:**

- Email: `security@ouryahoo.com` (or `tobala@yahooinc.com` for direct routing)
- Or use the private vulnerability report on GitHub Enterprise: [Security Advisories](https://git.ouryahoo.com/tobala/erp-api-token-manager/security/advisories/new)

**Response SLA:**

| Severity | Acknowledgement | Initial Assessment | Patch & Disclosure |
|----------|----------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Critical (RCE, auth bypass, data exfiltration) | 24 hours | 48 hours | **72 hours** |
| High (privilege escalation, info leak) | 48 hours | 5 business days | **7 days** |
| Medium (DoS, hardening gap) | 5 business days | 14 days | **90 days** |
| Low (best-practice deviation) | Best effort | 30 days | Next minor release |

We credit responsible disclosures in the release notes (with reporter consent). See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the full policy.
